newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says economic recovery starting to strengthen.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says economic recovery starting to strengthen.

text.p: Japan's economic recovery is starting to gain firmness, Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a news conference on Wednesday.
"Japan's economy is continuing its gradual recovery and the strength of the recovery is starting to increase," Matsushita said.

"We can well expect the positive mechanism to strengthen which centres upon the favourable cycle of increasing production leading to rising income and consumption, but we still need to keep watch (over whether this will happen)," he said.
"Our monetary policy for now is to place emphasis on securing the basis for economic recovery while keeping close watch over developments," he said.
Public spending has mostly peaked, but housing investment continues at high levels on demand triggered by the planned rise in the consumption tax in April, the governor said.
Corporate capital spending is basically recovering on the back of increasing corporate profits, the governor said.

Private consumption is regaining momentum after falling during the summer. A decline in net exports has generally come to a halt after the correction in the strengthening of the yen. Inventory adjustment in some materials industries has been progressing while the pace of production is speeding up, he said.

At the same time companies have not yet dropped their cautious attitude towards the prospects for the economy, which probably stems from structural adjustment pressures and worries over falling public expenditures, he said.
Concerning the U.S. economy, he said housing investment and private consumption have slowed slightly and that corporate capital investment, especially in the information industry, was steady.
Overall, the U.S. economy has slowed down temporarily but is still on a long-term recovery track. Interest rates are gradually rising but prices are generally stable, he said.
Asked about U.S. stock prices, he said he could not comment on specific price levels.
